chapter: Solo years, marriages and the Canadian party
title: Tangent on black suffering, education and Carter
summary: On Tape 12 he argues black people suffered under education and denounces Carter's human rights stance.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: ... and nobody knows you have any brains, and you go through all these things. (Unaudible) on that thing, biology, like Clarence (Muse) was talking about if they were sure he didn't have any brains, they wouldn't give him the job. The same thing happens when you got brains, you can't show your brains and get no job. No, uh-uh, you like to hide all the education you had to get a job and go through the things you wouldn't go through if you didn't have to do it. It's a mess. It's a mess. You talking about the negro sufferin', I don't think the negro has suffered as hard as the Jewish people have suffered. They had as much trouble to go through as we did, or more. But I don't think they had the education that the negro had to go through his. You see what I mean, that's the big difference. If the negro didn't have no education it wouldn't be hard. But he had the

education. It's like today, if you know -- my rights, my rights, my rights -- forget about my rights. All right, everybody's got a right to suffer the consequences and that's what those United States is going to be doin' shortly, suffering the consequences and Carter is the leader of it. They're going to put him again for another run for the President, you know that. He's going to run again. You know that, don't ya. And he's going to win this time, ain't that funny? Why? Because he's a puppet for the other countries. That's all. See, what kills him is coming out with that Human Rights. In my book, that kills him. Human Rights is a disgrace for this country to talk about -- Human Rights.
